newsitem.title: UK: NWE STRAIGHT-RUN FUEL STEADY WITH MOST CARGOES SOLD.
newsitem.headline: NWE STRAIGHT-RUN FUEL STEADY WITH MOST CARGOES SOLD.

text.p: European low sulphur straight-run was steady on Thursday with sellers standing their ground around the $115/$117 mark, saying more than half of the August cargoes have already been sold.
One refiner offered a 30,000-tonne August 29-31 loader at $115 fob while the asking price of two other sellers of 0.5-0.7 percent sulphur material was $2 higher.

"About 60 percent of cargoes are already gone...There has never been a time when you sell three weeks in advance and sellers don't like that so they are upping the price," a trader with a refiner said.
"The cargo I sold two weeks ago at $107 is lifting tomorrow and now the market is about $115," the trader added.
The fate of a cargo bought this week by an independent trader at $110/$111 and re-offered at $113 fob Sines on Wednesday was not immediately known.
Russian high sulphur straight-run continued to be offered at strong prices, with M-100 at premia of up to $6 to the two means quote but no fresh deals were heard.
There was unconfirmed talk of a deal at two means +$5.50 late on Wednesday.
